gaps.text: Combining several spectroscopy methods (data fusion) (Low-level fusion: synchronized NIR reflection and Raman spectra merged into one augmented matrix for a PLS-type model. Both probes must view the same belt spot and the data must be normalized to a common time step, with block scaling so neither method dominates. The fused model must beat the best single-method model on independent loads, otherwise the extra instrument is dropped.)
No supplied source describes spectroscopy of excavated or remediation soil; all precedents are dairy, pharma, bioprocess or tissue.
No source gives achievable accuracy, standoff distance or acquisition rate for reflection measurement of dark granular solids on a belt.
Dark, lumpy, strongly absorbing soil will still return a usable diffuse-reflection signal.

items.finding: Multi-sensor fusion does not automatically improve results, as effectiveness depends on mutual correction and complementarity among sensors rather than their sheer number.
items.how_it_applies: This suggests that before committing to a multi-method setup, testing should verify whether combining NIR and Raman actually improves predictions over a single method.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The cited study evaluated food and biological samples rather than heterogeneous excavated soil on an industrial conveyor belt, so complementarity may differ.

citation.quote: It is noteworthy that the effectiveness of multi-sensor fusion does not increase proportionally with the number of sensors; rather, it hinges on mutual correction and complementarity among different sensors.
citation.label: E05 ¶29

items.finding: Low-level data fusion rearranges data from different sources into a new augmented matrix where variables are placed sequentially.
items.how_it_applies: This provides a baseline approach for data alignment if synchronized NIR and Raman spectra are tested together on the belt.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: This concept comes from general pharmaceutical and analytical data reviews rather than a moving, lumpy solid material stream.

citation.quote: Low-level data fusion (LLDF) is considered the simplest method to achieve a combination of inputs. In this case, the data is rearranged into a new data matrix, where the variables coming from different sources are placed one after the other.
citation.label: E02 ¶31
